value: superclaude is one of the entry points that will start the ground loop but only if it's not already running. I also propose that the ground loop has a file it touches on each pass. can be in it's device space in .cairn. that shows us it's last run without scanning for the process. if we were really smart we'd put it's state in there too... and then when the web server displays the ground loop state in it's device, it's process ID would be present. process id as part of the base shim device status pane too.

The one resident process in Cairn reports its own liveness, so nothing has to go looking for it. The loop writes a record on each pass — last-run, state, pid — in its own device space. Every consumer (a start-guard, a status pane, a human) READS that record instead of scanning the process table. Liveness stops being a host question and becomes an owned fact (Law 6).

value.assumption_1: The ground loop is a RESIDENT PROCESS. Checked against NO DAEMONS and it is a distinction, not a collision: I-heartbeat-probes-and-bus.md already names the ground loop as 'the one permitted periodic pulse, and it exists precisely so that nothing else has to be.'
value.assumption_2_CORRECTED_2026-07-31: SUPERSEDED. I recorded this as 'a file that is touched tells us the loop is running — FALSE AS STATED.' Akien: 'a crashed loop does leave the file behind: BUT IT STOPS UPDATING THE TIMESTAMP. So then it's possible to DETECT that it's not running and start it.' Correct, and the detector was already in his design — he specified last-run in the file before I raised anything. The honest word was UNDERSPECIFIED, not false: the design was one number short, and the number is 5 seconds. Recording the miss because it is the third of a kind — I reach for the strong word (conflict, false) where the honest one is 'not yet specified'. See memory ask-the-why-to-distinguish, same failure direction, now n=3.
value.assumption_2_FALSE_AS_STATED: 'A file that is touched tells us the loop is running.' It does not — a crashed loop leaves the file behind. Akien's own design supplies the fix without connecting it: the record carries LAST RUN, so liveness is 'touched within N beats', not 'file exists'. Connecting those two halves is this ticket's real content.
value.collides: Checked four ways, no collision. NO DAEMONS: distinction (above). reaching-for-daemons-is-drift: a per-pass touch is the loop recording itself, not a poller; a reader that POLLED the file would be the drift, and every reader here is event-driven (a browser request, a launch). Law 6: the ground loop owns the file, in its own device space. system_rackmount owns host-resource predicates — and this design never asks the host anything, which sidesteps that ownership question rather than crossing it.
value.falsifiable: yes — stated above, both directions, with a horizon.
value.missing_2_the_race: Two entry points reading 'not running' at the same moment both start a loop. Read-then-act is not atomic; the claim must be (O_EXCL create, or equivalent). Carried by the child that owns the guard.
value.missing_3_the_skill_template_is_short_a_: MEASURED while casting this: /sorted's watchme template lists six fields (object, trigger, enough, carrier, nexus, consumer) but cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py — built TODAY under ticket watchme-emits-a-probe — requires a seventh, `probe`, naming the berth the emission gate resolves ARMED from. A ticket cast straight from the skill text refuses at the crossing. The physics is right and the skill text is stale; that is the good direction of drift (Law 4), but it is drift. IOU: update ~/.claude/skills/sorted/SKILL.md. Not done in this act — it is a different owner's artifact and gets its own small ticket rather than a drive-by edit.
value.verdict: CAST. The two missing points are specifiable implementation decisions, not open design, so they are named on the ticket rather than routed back. If Akien reads the staleness threshold as a design question, this reverts to a red and the parent goes back to THINKME.

value: THE STALENESS THRESHOLD IS 5 SECONDS — five missed ticks at the ruled once-per-second cadence. Ruled by Akien 2026-07-31. Three times the interval is the standard liveness heuristic; five gives slack for a loaded box without anyone noticing the lag. LIVE = last-run within 5s. DEAD = last-run older than 5s, whatever the file says about state, whatever pid it names. A crashed loop leaves the file behind but STOPS ADVANCING THE TIMESTAMP — that is the whole detector, and it is Akien's, present in the design from the first telling.

RETIRED — superseded by siblings that PROVED. The intention (the loop writes last-run/state/pid in its own device space; every consumer reads the record instead of scanning the process table) landed via ground-loop-writes-its-own-liveness [PROVED] (the ground_loop charter's edge (b) reads 'LANDED (ticket ground-loop-writes-its-own-liveness)') and the staleness direction via the-loop-names-its-own-staleness-instead-of-benching-a-device [PROVED]. The start-guard, the status pane, and probescan all read the liveness record today. This earlier cast was the same aim before it split into the two that sailed. Retirement is a FILING, not a crossing: the cursor stays where the voyage stopped, and the formal RETIRED disposition is owed physics — it is pending child (a) of ticket state-machine-physics ('dispositions (DROPPED / SUPERSEDED / RETIRED) fully specified'), which this filing cites rather than pre-empts.
